info.name: Notion Search — Engineering Issue Tracker
info.description:
Search + filter API over the Notion database **🛠️ Engineering Issue Tracker**.

### Setup
1. Start the server: `npm start` (defaults to `http://localhost:3100`).
2. Adjust the `baseUrl` collection variable if you run on another host/port.
3. **Run `01 · Health & metadata → Filter instructions` first.** Its test script captures `{{assigneeId}}`, `{{assigneeName}}`, `{{assigneeEmail}}`, `{{sprintId}}` and `{{sprintName}}`, which the *by id* and *by email* requests depend on.

The whole collection is safe to run with Postman's Collection Runner — every request is a read, nothing writes to Notion.

### Things worth knowing
- Values inside one parameter are **OR**-ed; different parameters are **AND**-ed.
- Notion cannot text-match `people` or `relation` columns, so assignee and sprint names are resolved to ids before filtering.
- Notion cannot see page **body** text or **comments** at all. Both are indexed by this server and matched in-process — see the paired requests in *02 · Text search*.
- Comment search reads *unresolved* comments only; Notion exposes no way to read a resolved thread.
- Unresolvable filter values return HTTP 200 with a `notice`, never a 4xx.

request.description: Liveness probe. Returns `{ ok: true }`.

item.name: Options — values for the form dropdowns

request.description: Compact value lists: assignees, sprints, statuses, priorities. Backs the four dropdowns in the web form.
Assignee/sprint values are cached for 5 minutes. `refresh=1` rebuilds the directory immediately — use after adding a sprint or a teammate.

**The filter capability API.** Self-describing: for every filterable field it returns the Notion property, the operators, the raw Notion filter template and the complete set of allowed values for **assignee** and **sprint**.

Its test script stores `{{assigneeId}}`, `{{assigneeName}}`, `{{assigneeEmail}}`, `{{sprintId}}` and `{{sprintName}}` as collection variables, so run it once before the *by id* / *by email* requests further down.

item.name: Filter instructions — force a cache refresh

request.description: Same document, rebuilt from Notion rather than served from the 5-minute cache.

item.name: All tasks — no filter at all

request.description: No parameters means no filter: every row, newest edit first. `total` is the real count, not the page size.

item.name: Free text across all default fields

request.description:
Case-insensitive `contains` over Assignee, Description, Summary, Sprint, Task Name, Dependencies, Story ID **and the page body**.

Check `matched_fields` on each row to see which field actually hit.

item.name: Text that lives ONLY in the page body

request.description:
`"not-found response"` appears in no property — only inside the body of task #4.

A Notion database query can never see page body text, so this server indexes the block tree of every page and matches it in-process. The row comes back with `matched_fields: ["page_content"]` and a highlighted excerpt.

item.name: Same term with page_content OFF — proves Notion alone cannot find it

request.description: Identical search minus the `page_content` field, i.e. pure Notion-side behaviour. Returns **0 results** — this is exactly why a property-only search was missing rows.
`fields` narrows what `q` searches. Allowed keys: assignee, description, summary, sprint, task_name, dependencies, story_id, source_team, source_type, page_content.

item.name: Search the assignee column by name

request.description: Notion cannot text-match a `people` column. The term is resolved against the user directory first, then filtered by user id. `text_matching.notion_filter_equivalent` shows the id-based filter that was actually evaluated.

item.name: Search the sprint column by name

request.description: Same trick for the `relation` column: sprint name → page id → `relation.contains`.

Searches comment threads on each task page.

Comments are not a database property, so Notion cannot filter on them — this server reads them via `GET /v1/comments` and matches in-process. Matching rows return only the threads that hit, each with an excerpt, author and timestamp, plus `comment_count` for the page total.

**Limitation:** Notion's API returns *unresolved* comments only. Once a thread is resolved in the UI it is no longer readable through the API and cannot be searched.

Check `text_matching.comment.comments_indexed` in the response — if it is 0, the workspace genuinely has no unresolved comments.
The two non-property sources combined. `matched_fields` tells you which one hit.
Baseline for comparing against the comments-only search above.
Only the indexed page-body text. Useful for acceptance criteria and API details, which live in the body rather than in any property.
Prefix search over the Story ID column.

item.name: Include the opt-in fields (Source Team / Source Type)

request.description: `source_team` and `source_type` are off by default; name them explicitly to search them.
Matching is case-insensitive on both the Notion side and in the body index — this returns the same total as the lowercase `supplier` search.
Empty result set, `total: 0`, HTTP 200 — not an error.
Accepts a partial, case-insensitive name. Resolved to a user id before filtering.

The exact form Notion itself uses: `{ property: "Assignees", people: { contains: <uuid> } }`.

Requires **Filter instructions** to have run first. This is the only way to filter the workspace guest whose name the integration cannot read.
Emails resolve through the same directory lookup as names.
`none` (or `unassigned`) maps to `people.is_empty: true`.
Repeated/comma-separated values inside one parameter are OR-ed together.

item.name: Unknown assignee → notice, not a crash

request.description: Unresolvable value returns HTTP 200 with an empty result set and a `notice` pointing at `/api/filters`.
`{ property: "Sprint", relation: { contains: <page_id> } }`. Requires **Filter instructions** to have run first.
Comma-separated values are OR-ed.
Maps to `relation.is_empty: true`.
Same graceful handling as an unknown assignee.
Exact status name. Full list comes from `/api/options`.
Different parameters are AND-ed; values inside one parameter are OR-ed.
Text AND assignee AND sprint AND status. Inspect `notion_filter` in the response to see the exact filter object sent to Notion.
Finds rows that slipped through triage.
Take `next_cursor` from the response and pass it as `offset` for the next page.
`offset` and `start_cursor` are accepted interchangeably.
100 is the ceiling.
No error — the value is clamped.

item.name: POST — same options as the query string

request.description: `POST /api/search` accepts the identical keys as JSON. Arrays are OR-ed, which avoids escaping commas in values.

item.name: POST — arrays for assignee and status

request.description: `fields` may also be an array here.
No keys means no filter.
Unrecognised keys in `fields` are dropped; the valid ones still apply.

item.name: Empty q behaves as no text filter

request.description: A blank `q` is ignored, leaving only the structured filters.
Express default 404 — confirms you are hitting the right server.
